notes: Synthetic teaching inputs. No observed quotes, holdings, or price history. Not market-performance evidence.

Entries overlap: each trade shares days with 5 of its neighbours, so the significance test flips signs a block at a time and the interval resamples blocks. Treating these as 134 independent trades would understate the standard error by roughly a factor of two.
the permutation test cannot distinguish this result from a rule with no edge

statistics.accounting: one unit of capital at risk per trade, returns summed rather than compounded, so the curve and the drawdown are in units of per-trade risk

significance.null: the sign of each block of overlapping trades is arbitrary, which is what a rule with no edge produces
significance.caveat: A p-value is only a p-value for a hypothesis chosen before seeing the data. A rule selected because its backtest looked good has already spent its degrees of freedom, and this number then understates how easily the result could be chance.
